title-group.article-title: Stability of Perovskite Films under Thermal Cycling: The Role of Organic Additives

trans-title-group.trans-title: Стабильность перовскитных плёнок при термоциклировании: роль органических добавок

abstract.p: Halide perovskites are regarded as one of the most promising materials for thin-film photovoltaics, but their practical use is held back by insufficient stability under the temperature fluctuations typical of real operating conditions. This study examines the effect of three organic additives, phenethylammonium, thiourea and polyvinylpyrrolidone, on the degradation of mixed-cation perovskite films under thermal cycling between −20 and +85 °C. Films were prepared by antisolvent-assisted spin coating and characterised by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy and photoluminescence spectroscopy after 0, 50, 100 and 200 cycles. In control samples, a lead iodide phase appears after only 100 cycles, microcracks form along grain boundaries, and photoluminescence intensity drops by almost half. Adding phenethylammonium at 1.5 mol% slows degradation: after 200 cycles, 87% of the initial photoluminescence intensity is retained and no secondary phases are detected. Thiourea increases grain size but has little effect on resistance to thermal cycling, whereas polyvinylpyrrolidone effectively suppresses cracking. A mechanism is proposed that links the stabilising effect of the additives to the passivation of surface defects and the relaxation of mechanical stress. The results can inform the development of formulations for flexible solar modules.

trans-abstract.p: Галогенидные перовскиты рассматриваются как один из наиболее перспективных материалов для тонкоплёночной фотовольтаики, однако их практическое применение сдерживается недостаточной стабильностью при перепадах температуры, характерных для реальных условий эксплуатации. В работе исследовано влияние трёх органических добавок — фенилэтиламмония, тиомочевины и поливинилпирролидона — на деградацию плёнок смешанного катионного перовскита при термоциклировании в диапазоне от −20 до +85 °C. Плёнки получены методом центрифугирования с антирастворителем и охарактеризованы методами рентгеновской дифракции, сканирующей электронной микроскопии и спектроскопии фотолюминесценции после 0, 50, 100 и 200 циклов. Установлено, что в контрольных образцах уже после 100 циклов появляется фаза иодида свинца и формируются микротрещины по границам зёрен, а интенсивность фотолюминесценции снижается почти вдвое. Добавление фенилэтиламмония в концентрации 1,5 мол. % замедляет деградацию: после 200 циклов сохраняется 87 % исходной интенсивности фотолюминесценции, а образование побочных фаз не обнаруживается. Тиомочевина увеличивает размер зёрен, но слабо влияет на устойчивость к термоциклированию, тогда как поливинилпирролидон эффективно подавляет растрескивание. Предложен механизм, связывающий стабилизирующее действие добавок с пассивацией поверхностных дефектов и релаксацией механических напряжений. Результаты могут быть использованы при разработке составов для гибких солнечных модулей.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Over the past fifteen years, the power conversion efficiency of perovskite solar cells has risen from a few per cent to values comparable with those of silicon cells. The main obstacle to commercialisation remains stability: under the action of moisture, light and temperature, the perovskite crystal lattice decomposes with the formation of lead iodide.

Thermal cycling — repeated temperature changes — is one of the most severe tests, since the mismatch between the thermal expansion coefficients of the film and the substrate leads to the accumulation of mechanical stress. The aim of the study is to compare the effectiveness of three organic additives of different nature in improving the resistance of films to thermal cycling.

sec.title: Materials and Methods
sec.p: Films of a mixed-cation perovskite based on caesium, formamidinium and methylammonium (CsFAMA) with partial substitution of iodine by bromine (15%) were deposited on glass substrates with a conductive coating by spin coating with dropwise addition of an antisolvent and annealed at 100 °C. The additives were introduced into the precursor solution: phenethylammonium iodide (PEA, 1.5 mol%), thiourea (TU, 3 mol%) and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP, 0.5 wt%).

Thermal cycling was carried out in a climatic chamber under an inert atmosphere: one cycle comprised a 15-min dwell at −20 °C and a 15-min dwell at +85 °C with a temperature ramp rate of 5 °C/min. After 0, 50, 100 and 200 cycles, the samples were examined by X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy and steady-state photoluminescence.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: The change in integrated photoluminescence intensity as a function of the number of cycles is shown in Fig. 1. In the control samples, the intensity decreases to 54% of the initial value after 100 cycles and to 31% after 200 cycles; at the same time, a lead iodide reflection at 2θ = 12.7° appears in the diffraction patterns.

caption.p: Fig. 1. Relative photoluminescence intensity of the films as a function of the number of thermal cycles, %

sec.p: The highest stability was demonstrated by the PEA films, in which no secondary phases were detected even after 200 cycles. The addition of PVP almost completely suppresses the formation of microcracks but does not prevent a gradual decrease in photoluminescence intensity. Summary characteristics are given in Table 1.

caption.p: Table 1. Characteristics of the films before and after 200 cycles

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: The stabilising effect of PEA can be explained by the formation of a thin layer of two-dimensional perovskite on the grain surfaces, which passivates defects and hinders the migration of halide ions. PVP apparently acts differently: polymer chains localised at the grain boundaries partially relax mechanical stresses and prevent cracking.

The difference in mechanisms opens up the possibility of using the additives in combination. Preliminary experiments with the simultaneous introduction of PEA and PVP show retention of 91% of the photoluminescence intensity after 200 cycles, which requires further verification in complete solar cells.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: Phenethylammonium is the most effective of the additives studied for improving the resistance of perovskite films to thermal cycling, while polyvinylpyrrolidone effectively suppresses cracking. Combining additives with different mechanisms of action appears to be a promising strategy.
